classification.difficultyReason: Substitute expressions between two linear equations, including negative coefficients and exact fractional solutions.

content.prompt: Solve the simultaneous equations using the substitution method.

answer.worked:
Substitute $x=3y+2$ into $y=x-6$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=3y+2-6\\y&=3y-4\\-2y&=-4\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
Substitute $y=2$ into $x=3y+2$.
$$\begin{align*}x&=3(2)+2\\x&=8\end{align*}$$
Check: $8=3(2)+2$ and $2=8-6$.
Hence $x=8$ and $y=2$.

Substitute $x=2y-1$ into $2x+y=11$.
$$\begin{align*}2(2y-1)+y&=11\\4y-2+y&=11\\5y-2&=11\\5y&=13\\y&=\frac{13}{5}\end{align*}$$
Substitute $y=\frac{13}{5}$ into $x=2y-1$.
$$\begin{align*}x&=2\left(\frac{13}{5}\right)-1\\x&=\frac{21}{5}\end{align*}$$
Check: $\frac{21}{5}=2\left(\frac{13}{5}\right)-1$ and $2\left(\frac{21}{5}\right)+\frac{13}{5}=11$.
Hence $x=\frac{21}{5}$ and $y=\frac{13}{5}$.

Substitute $x=y-3$ into $x=3y-13$.
$$\begin{align*}y-3&=3y-13\\10&=2y\\y&=5\end{align*}$$
Substitute $y=5$ into $x=y-3$.
$$\begin{align*}x&=5-3\\x&=2\end{align*}$$
Check: $2=5-3$ and $2=3(5)-13$.
Hence $x=2$ and $y=5$.

Substitute $y=3x-2$ into $x=2y+3$.
$$\begin{align*}x&=2(3x-2)+3\\x&=6x-4+3\\x&=6x-1\\-5x&=-1\\x&=\frac{1}{5}\end{align*}$$
Substitute $x=\frac{1}{5}$ into $y=3x-2$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=3\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)-2\\y&=-\frac{7}{5}\end{align*}$$
Check: $-\frac{7}{5}=3\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)-2$ and $\frac{1}{5}=2\left(-\frac{7}{5}\right)+3$.
Hence $x=\frac{1}{5}$ and $y=-\frac{7}{5}$.
